notes: Fiscal year ended June 30, 2024 (matches data.js fy 'Jun 2024'). Financial figures are from the FY2024 Form 10-K (accession 0000950170-24-087843) and checked against SEC XBRL. OWNERSHIP: the proxy published after that fiscal year (DEF 14A filed October 24, 2024, accession 0001193125-24-242883) lists beneficial ownership only for current directors, nominees and named executives, plus holders above 5%. Bill Gates is in neither table (he is not a director or named executive), so his stake is not reported in the company's filings: status no-reported-stake, values null. Nothing is filled from other sources. The two 5% holders' percentages are the proxy's 'Percent of Class to be Voted During the Meeting', based on Schedule 13G/A filings dated February 13, 2024; the proxy gives the filing date but not the date those holdings refer to, so asOf is null. Directors and executive officers as a group held 2,330,484 shares (less than 1%). BUYBACKS: the $17,254 million cash-flow line includes about $5.3 billion of shares repurchased to settle employee tax withholding on vesting stock awards; the 10-K's repurchase-program table, which excludes those, totals $11,960 million for fiscal 2024. GEOGRAPHY: 'United States' includes billings to OEMs and certain multinational organizations (10-K footnote a).

source.quote: According to IDC, for every $1 of Microsoft revenue, services partners earn $8.45, and software partners earn $10.93. … *IDC: Microsoft Partners: Driving Economic Value and AI Maturity

ecosystem.notes: Microsoft's FY2024 10-K has no flow measure for its partner ecosystem, so measure and platformRevenue are null. The only figure is an IDC multiplier (partner revenue per $1 of Microsoft revenue), which is a ratio, so value is null and both ratios are kept in the claim. The IDC study could not be fetched. The Microsoft partner-blog article that presented it (partner.microsoft.com/.../ai-value-for-partners) now 302-redirects to an author page. commissionedBy is null because no fetched document states who paid for the study. The Microsoft blog cites only the IDC title. A Microsoft Tech Community post fetched this session calls it 'A March 2025 IDC study', which conflicts with other dating, so year is null. The IDC multiplier is partner revenue, not money paid by Microsoft.
